title: Exponential Functions: Growth and Decay
seo_title: Algebra I Exponential Functions Worksheets (TEKS A.9C)
standard_text: A.9B interpret the meaning of the values of a and b in exponential functions of the form f(x) = ab^x in real-world problems; A.9C write exponential functions in the form f(x) = ab^x (where b is a rational number) to describe problems arising from mathematical and real-world situations, including growth and decay; A.9D graph exponential functions that model growth and decay and identify key features, including y-intercept and asymptote, in mathematical and real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Algebra I worksheets for Texas TEKS A.9B–A.9D: exponential growth and decay, the meaning of a and b, writing f(x) = ab^x, compound interest and graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: f(x) = ab^x: a starts it, b multiplies it.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • In f(x) = abx, a is the starting value and b is the growth factor.
  • b > 1: growth. 0 < b < 1: decay.
  • Growth by r percent: b = 1 + r. Decay by r percent: b = 1 − r.
  • The graph has y-intercept a and never touches the x-axis.

Examples

Example

$500 grows 4% a year

b = 1.04

Answer: f(t) = 500(1.04)t

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying a and b firstRaise b to the power, then multiply by a.
Using r instead of 1 + r4% growth is 1.04.
Calling 0.8 growthb < 1 is decay.
